- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 2+ consecutive +0.20+), model underreacts; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment.
- Model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for days 25–30 of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; anchor forecast to 3–5-day moving average of history.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of negative sentiment duration.
